title: Serre-subcategory property (S) — a consequence, not a hypothesis
body_html:
Serre-subcategory property (S) — a consequence, not a hypothesis

In earlier formulations of this framework, the Serre-subcategory property $$\textup{(S):}\quad \Rep_\Phi(G) \subseteq \Rep(G) \text{ is closed under subobjects, quotients, and extensions}$$ was assumed as a separate hypothesis (used to lift a per-irreducible acyclicity argument to arbitrary $V \in \Rep_\Phi(G)$ in the contraction-based §7.1 resolution argument).

Under the cartesian-cosheaf framework (following Lanard; Lanard's depth-zero block equivalence and Cartesian cosheaves Cosh^cart_G(X,R,φ) and unit isomorphism), (S) is automatic: it follows as a corollary of the cartesian equivalence.

Statement

Proposition ((S) as a consequence). Assume (T1)–(T5), (K1)–(K2), and $K_x$-local (A1) (verified for parahoric / classical / tame in [[node:building.A1_Kx_local_verifications]]). Then $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ is a Serre subcategory of $\Rep(G)$ stable under arbitrary direct sums.
proof_html:
By the cartesian equivalence theorem (Cartesian cosheaves Cosh^cart_G(X,R,φ) and unit isomorphism Thm), $\Loc_\phi$ induces an equivalence $$\Rep_\Phi(G) \;\simeq\; \mathrm{Cosh}^{\mathrm{cart}}_G(\BSigma, R, \phi).$$

The right-hand category is visibly a Serre subcategory of $\mathrm{Cosh}_G(\BSigma, R, \phi)$ (defined by a restriction-map condition preserved under sub/quot/ext), and the latter is a Serre subcategory of $\mathrm{Cosh}_G(\BSigma, R)$ (depth-restriction at each facet). Transporting this Serre structure across the equivalence, $\Rep_\Phi(G) \subseteq \Rep(G)$ is a Serre subcategory.

Closure under arbitrary direct sums: same argument applied to direct sums (which are preserved by $\Loc_\phi$ and $H_0$). $\square$

Status change

Era (S) status
Pre-Lanard (Sheaf7 §7.1) Hypothesis; required for global resolution
Cartesian framework (this paper) Corollary of Thm cartesian-equivalence

This is a clean reduction in hypothesis count, as the audit in [HYPOTHESIS_AUDIT.md] anticipated under the Lanard switch.

Historical note (per-application verifications no longer needed)

The previous per-application verifications of (S) (which existed when (S) was a hypothesis):

  • Classical: $[HKSS, Prop 6.7]$ — see Hypothesis (S) for classical groups via [HKSS].
  • Tame: Bernstein decomposition + $[KY, Thm 6.3]$ — see Hypothesis (S) for tame types via Bernstein + [KY].

These verifications are now redundant for the main framework (they were specific to the hypothesis-driven formulation). The applications nodes are kept for historical reference but the main chain no longer needs them.

  • Lanard's depth-zero block equivalence — Lanard's framework.
